children: Price Formulation
价格构式
Hic Rhodus, hic salta

We have arrived at the decisive moment. Let us imagine that goods have been pass(act)ivated, qualculative agencies equipped, meeting sites distributed, regulated, and arranged. Furthermore, let us imagine that attachment, detachment, and consent to pay have been obtained through the skillful promotion and management of affects. All that is left is to craft a price.
Hic Rhodus, hic salta
!（此地即罗得岛，就在此地跳吧！）
我们已经来到决定性的时刻。让我们设想：物品已被被动化—激活，质算能动者已装备齐全，相遇场所已被分配、规制与安排。再让我们设想：通过巧妙地促进与管理情动，附着、脱离以及对支付的同意都已获得。剩下的，就只是打造一个价格了。

Crafting prices does not interrupt the continuity of the previous framings. It is inscribed in the long and tortuous process through which goods and agencies are singularized. Recall Las Vegas and its slot machines. First, chance had to be domesticated, produced on demand in the discrete form of an association of figures on separate reels, moved by complex algorithms and set off at the simple push of a button. Gamblers had to seat themselves facing this organized production of random configurations flashing onto a digital screen as though coming from nowhere. Future gamblers had to be nudged toward the airports from which cheap flights take off to the gambling capital, then guided to the machines that would assist them in their calculations and decisions. An atmosphere had to be created, a succession of screens orchestrated, so as to lead these gamblers to gradually forget the outside world, all for the pleasure of continuing to play. Carried away by this force, abandoning themselves to it, the gamblers had only one thing to do: pay, then press a button so the motion would go on and they could remain playthings of chance.

打造价格并不会中断此前各项框定的连续性。它铭刻在物品与能动者被独一化的漫长而曲折的过程之中。回想一下拉斯维加斯及其老虎机。首先，必须驯化偶然性，按需生产它：其离散形式是分别位于各个独立转轮上的图形组合，由复杂算法驱动，只需按一下按钮便可启动。赌徒必须坐下面向这种对随机构型的组织化生产——这些构型在数字屏幕上闪烁，仿佛不知从何而来。未来的赌徒必须被轻轻推向那些机场，从那里有廉价航班飞往赌城，然后被引导至那些将协助他们计算与决策的机器。必须营造一种氛围，编排一连串屏幕，以便引导这些赌徒逐渐忘记外部世界，而这一切都是为了继续玩下去的快乐。赌徒被这股力量席卷，沉溺其中，他们只有一件事可做：付钱，然后按下按钮，让运动继续，好让他们继续做偶然性的玩物。
What all of the slot machine designers in the world have learned is that once consent to pay has been obtained, there are a thousand ways to obtain the payment of a
certain

sum. Some gamblers prefer to win big or lose big and cut the trip short. Others prefer a long, slow process of falling asleep: they press the button often, repeat the liberating gesture many times, win a bit, lose a bit, to make it last, enjoy for as long as possible the state of weightlessness whose pleasures and charms Michel Butor described so well in his novel
La modification
全世界的老虎机设计者都学到了一点：一旦取得支付的同意，就有千百种方式获得
某一
数额的付款。有些赌徒喜欢大赢或大输，迅速结束这场旅程。另一些人则偏爱漫长而缓慢的入睡过程：他们频繁按键，多次重复这一解放性的手势，赢一点，输一点，为的是让过程延续下去，尽可能长久地享受那种失重状态——米歇尔·布托（Michel Butor）在其小说《变》（
La modification
）中对此种状态的乐趣与魅力作了精彩的描绘。

Is the price a gambler pays really determined by comparing supply and demand? One can say this, of course, but the explanation comes up rather short. When he finds himself in a situation where he is face to face with the machine, the gambler has been acted on as much as he has acted. Over the course of this journey, the constitution of supply and demand have become so entangled that it would be useless to try to introduce a sharp distinction between them. Moreover, and this is why the gambling situation is so interesting, price is an essential component of this service. It is a strategic variable that determines its quality, not the reverse. By choosing a price level (such a stake, at such a rhythm), the gambler sets the conditions for the experience to be a success, in that he sets the conditions that will make him quiver or founder. The price thus participates forcefully in the qualification of the good. It is a quality of the good. It does not measure the good’s value.

赌徒所支付的价格，真的由供给与需求的比较决定吗？当然可以这样说，但这一解释未免过于单薄。当赌徒发现自己面对机器时，他既采取了行动，也同样受到了作用。在这段旅程中，供给与需求的构成已如此纠缠在一起，以至于试图在二者之间引入明确区分将是徒劳的。此外——这也正是赌博情境如此有趣的原因——价格是这项服务的一个本质组成部分。它是一个决定服务品质的战略变量，而不是相反。通过选择某一价格水平（如此这般的赌注，以如此这般的节奏），赌徒为这场体验的成功设定了条件，因为他设定了使自己颤抖或崩溃的条件。因此，价格有力地参与了物品的品质界定。它是物品的一种品质。它并不衡量物品的价值。

In this chapter, I will argue that what is obvious in the case of the gambling industries is true for other commercial sectors. Pricing does not come after the goods’ qualification; rather, the pricing process feeds and prolongs that qualification. To underline this reversal, I suggest we think in terms of
price formulation

. This notion emphasizes the fact that a price is not determined at some moment at which supply and demand are supposed to meet. It is the result of a process that often begins very early, when a good is still only a vague idea in a design studio or a research lab. It also highlights that establishing the price is a strategic variable around which power relations are formed and through which the establishment of bilateral monopolies is at stake.
在本章中，我将论证：在赌博业中显而易见的事情，对其他商业部门同样成立。定价并不发生在物品的品质界定之后；相反，定价过程滋养并延长了那种品质界定。为强调这一颠倒，我建议我们以价格构式（
price formulation
）来思考。这一概念强调：价格并不是在供给与需求本应相遇的某一时刻被确定的。它是一个过程的结果，而这个过程往往开始得很早，那时一件物品还只是设计工作室或研究实验室里的一个模糊想法。它还凸显出，确定价格是一个战略变量：权力关系围绕它而形成，双边垄断的建立亦系于它。

This chapter should serve as an introduction to the analysis of price formulation in market agencements, a task that requires a particular theoretical effort. Few studies are actually useful to me, other than a growing set of empirical studies made in the last few years, which will provide precious help. This analysis also requires making some inroads into the black box of how agents calculate prices, which is not always easy to grasp and explain. We must follow agencies in their work as they design and implement the different formulations that allow them to establish prices and to ensure these prices will be accepted. Since the inversions with respect to traditional approaches are most manifest in this chapter, I will begin by giving a detailed picture of the usual explanations of pricing. This will lead me to draw attention to the concept of a
discriminating monopoly

, a concept that will be useful for showing how prices participate both in establishing (singularized) bilateral transactions and in multiplying them. The notion of price formulation that I am introducing provides a new analysis of the relations of domination that cut across commercial activities.

本章应当作为对市场装配中价格构式之分析的导论；这项任务需要付出特殊的理论努力。实际上对我有用的研究寥寥无几，唯有近些年日渐增多的一批经验研究将提供宝贵的帮助。这一分析还要求我们深入行动者如何计算价格这一黑箱，而它并不总是容易把握和解释。我们必须追随能动者的工作，看他们如何设计并实施不同的构式，从而确立价格并确保这些价格被接受。由于相对于传统进路的颠倒在本章表现得最为明显，我将先详细描绘关于定价的通行解释。这将引导我关注歧视性垄断（
discriminating monopoly
）这一概念；该概念有助于表明，价格如何既参与建立（独一化的）双边交易，又参与使这类交易成倍增加。我所引入的价格构式概念，为贯穿商业活动的支配关系提供了一种新的分析。
THEORIES OF PRICING IN INTERFACE MARKETS
界面市场中的定价理论

Theories of pricing are generally conceived of for markets whose architecture is presumed to resemble the interface market model — that is, markets with disjoined supplies and demands, platform goods, and competition for those goods. These theories usually combine two opposing approaches. The first can be related to standard microeconomics, which considers that markets constitute a machinery whose principal virtue is that it eliminates power relations in favor of a collective calculation that reaches an optimal compromise on prices by taking into account the position and expectation of each agent. The second approach, developed mainly by the new economic sociology, contests this hypothesis and endeavors to show that pricing depends on the structure of social relations and the balance of power it imposes. Despite their divergences, both methods consider that price levels are determined by markets and the way they function.

定价理论通常是为这样一些市场而构想的：人们假定其架构类似于界面市场模型——即供给与需求彼此分离、存在平台物品、并围绕这些物品展开竞争的市场。这些理论通常把两种相互对立的进路结合起来。第一种可与标准微观经济学相联系：它认为市场构成一部机器，其主要优点在于消除权力关系，代之以一种集体计算，这种计算通过考虑每个行动者的位置与预期，就价格达成最优妥协。第二种进路主要由新经济社会学发展而来，它质疑这一假设，并力图表明定价取决于社会关系的结构以及这种结构所强加的力量平衡。尽管存在分歧，两种方法都认为价格水平由市场及其运作方式决定。
STANDARD MICROECONOMICS

According to standard microeconomics, prices are or should be jointly calculated by agents and the markets. To clarify this point, we should start from the bilateral transaction, the reference situation that the invention of interface markets tends to use as a starting point, if only to immediately push it into the background.
标准微观经济学
按照标准微观经济学的看法，价格是由行动者与市场共同计算的，或者应当如此。为阐明这一点，我们应当从双边交易出发——界面市场的发明倾向于把这一参照情境当作起点，哪怕只是为了随即把它推到背景之中。

In a bilateral transaction, which consists of a seller S, a buyer B, and a good at stake in the transaction, all the possible calculations are made by the agents. The necessary calculating skills are elementary, but very strict. It must be the case, and it suffices, that S knows the price (
Ps
) above which he will accept to sell and that B knows the price (
Pb
) above which he will refuse to buy.
The transaction will have a strong chance of success if
Ps ≤ Pb
since in that case, whichever price is finally chosen, everyone will be a winner. Let’s define
G
as
Pb – Ps
. If
G = Pb – Ps
is > 0, there exist many possible prices between
Ps
and
Pb
. Each of these prices corresponds to a certain sharing of
G

between the two agents. Which price is finally agreed upon depends on negotiation, on the bargaining between the two agents and, therefore on the power relations, which include, notably, but not solely, rhetorical skills, blackmail, better information, power positions, custom, manipulation of cognitive mechanisms (such as the framing of the negotiation by the first price mentioned), and more. Thus, in a bilateral transaction, pricing is a result of some combination of calculating activities and the balance of power.
在一笔双边交易中——它由卖方 S、买方 B 以及交易中作为利害所在的物品构成——所有可能的计算都由行动者完成。所需计算技能是初等的，但极其严格。必须满足、也只需满足：S 知道高于哪个价格他便愿意出售（
Ps
），B 知道高于哪个价格他便拒绝购买（
Pb
若
Ps ≤ Pb
，交易便很有可能成功，因为在此情况下，无论最终选定哪个价格，双方都是赢家。设
G
为
Pb – Ps
。若
G = Pb – Ps
> 0，则在
Ps
与
Pb
之间存在许多可能的价格。其中每一个价格都对应
G
在两个行动者之间的某种分配。最终商定哪个价格，取决于谈判，取决于两个行动者之间的讨价还价，因而也取决于权力关系——这些权力关系尤其包括（但不限于）修辞技巧、讹诈、更佳的信息、权力位置、习俗、对认知机制的操纵（例如以首先报出的价格来框定谈判），等等。因此，在双边交易中，定价是计算活动与力量平衡以某种方式结合的产物。

Those who defend interface markets cannot but deny the centrality of the bilateral transaction. Indeed, it is easy to understand that by increasing the number of agents (that is to say, of buyers and sellers), one increases the probability of seeing different values for
Ps
and
Pb

proliferate. Because the interface market intensifies the degree of competition, it is thus charged with progressively wiping out what comes down to power relations and their negotiation in establishing prices: at any moment, the bilateral negotiation can be interrupted and reframed by a third party, whether buyer or seller. Speaking phenomenologically, one can say that the stronger the pressure exerted by the market, the lower the chance that bargaining among agents can become established: it is the market that bargains. With the establishment of the interface market, which makes it possible to confront distinct and independent blocks, calculation is generalized and extended. The calculation ensured by markets, which can be compared to a giant price calculating machine, is added to the calculation ensured by agents. This moves us from the combination
price = calculation by B and by S + power relations
to the combination
price = calculation by B and S + calculation by the market
为界面市场辩护的人，不能不否认双边交易的中心性。的确，很容易理解：增加行动者（也就是买方与卖方）的数量，就会提高
Ps
与
Pb

出现众多不同取值的概率。由于界面市场强化了竞争程度，它因而被赋予这样的任务：逐步消除在价格确立中归结为权力关系及其协商的东西；在任何时刻，双边谈判都可能被第三方——无论买方还是卖方——打断并重新框定。从现象学角度说，可以这样讲：市场施加的压力越强，行动者之间的讨价还价得以确立的机会就越小——讨价还价的是市场本身。随着界面市场的建立——它使彼此不同而相互独立的板块得以正面相对——计算被普遍化并得到扩展。市场所确保的计算（可以比作一台巨型价格计算机）被添加到行动者所确保的计算之上。这就使我们从“
价格＝B 与 S 的计算＋权力关系
”这一组合，转向“
价格＝B 与 S 的计算＋市场的计算
”这一组合。

One of the ambitions of microeconomic theory is to study in detail the conditions under which information (notably about goods) is organized and revealed and circulates such that the market can take on the role it should play in discovering prices. The ideal is that the intervention of calculating agents (affixing
Ps
and
Pb
) will be reduced to its minimal, but strategic and morally just expression.
微观经济理论的一项抱负，是详细研究信息（尤其是关于物品的信息）在何种条件下被组织、被揭示并流通，从而使市场能够承担它在发现价格方面应当扮演的角色。理想状态是：进行计算的行动者（确定
Ps
与
Pb
）的干预，将被缩减到最小、然而具有战略意义且道德上正当的程度。

The war declared on the ever-possible prominence of bilateral transactions never ends because agents overflow with malice and inventiveness in order to impose these transactions as the rule. That is no doubt one of the reasons why economic theory has taken an increasing interest in the intermediary configurations that I propose to call
paucilateral

, configurations in which there are only a small number of agents and take place between the multilateral and the bilateral ones — that is, between situations of strong competition and situations that can be described as monopoly/monopsony. Inaugurated by Cournot’s duopoly theory

and extended by game theory, this approach makes it possible to understand how agents organize in order to formulate prices and how the strategies followed can lead them closer to or further from the price levels obtained in a situation of strong competition.
针对双边交易随时可能重新占据突出地位这一点所发动的战争永无终结，因为行动者满怀恶意与创造力，力图把这些交易强加为常规。这无疑正是经济理论日益关注我所提议称为“少边”（
paucilateral
）的中间构型的原因之一：这类构型中行动者数量很少，位于多边构型与双边构型之间——也就是处于强竞争情境与可称为垄断/买方垄断的情境之间。这一进路由古诺（Cournot）的双头垄断理论
开创，并由博弈论加以扩展；它使人能够理解，行动者如何组织起来以构式价格，以及他们所遵循的策略如何使他们更接近或更远离强竞争情境下得到的价格水平。

This analysis can be extended. Economist William Baumol and his academic and industrial allies redefined the very notion of bilateral transactions through the theory of contestable markets. Under certain conditions, this theory makes it possible to show that a situation of bilateral transaction (say, a monopoly) can be considered equivalent to a situation of multilateral relations: prices are calculated as though there were many buyers and sellers, since if the agents engaged in the transaction abuse their monopoly position, legions of agents will unfailingly appear, attracted by the lure of profit, thus reestablishing the calculating power of the markets.

这一分析可以进一步扩展。经济学家威廉·鲍莫尔（William Baumol）及其学术界与产业界的盟友，通过可竞争市场（contestable markets）理论重新界定了双边交易这一概念本身。在一定条件下，该理论能够表明，双边交易的情境（譬如垄断）可以被视为等同于多边关系的情境：价格仿佛是在有许多买方与卖方的情况下被计算出来的，因为倘若参与交易的行动者滥用其垄断地位，大批行动者定会受利润诱惑而出现，从而重建市场的计算能力。
ECONOMIC SOCIOLOGY

Economic sociology has not shown much interest in the question of pricing. When it has, it has generally been to underline that situations in which prices determined through a simple confrontation between supplies and demands, external to one another, constitute an exception. Indeed, beyond the faceoff between sellers and customers lurks the invisible and complicated web of social relations, a web that formats their meetings and imposes its logic. In economic sociology, to understand how prices are formed means starting from a very general hypothesis called
embedding

that asserts that agents are never isolated. Rather, they are always connected to one another. Following Jens Beckert’s interesting article on this subject, one can distinguish four different forms of embedding and therefore four different sociological interpretations of price formation mechanisms.
经济社会学
这一学科对定价问题并未表现出多少兴趣。当它表现出兴趣时，通常也是为了强调：价格由彼此外在的供给与需求之间的简单对峙所决定的情境，只是一种例外。的确，在卖方与顾客的对峙背后，潜伏着社会关系那张看不见的复杂之网；这张网塑造了他们的相会，并强加自己的逻辑。在经济社会学中，理解价格如何形成，意味着从一个非常一般的假设出发；这个假设叫作嵌入（
embedding
），它断言行动者从来不是孤立的，而始终彼此相连。循着延斯·贝克特（Jens Beckert）就此主题所写的一篇有趣文章，可以区分四种不同的嵌入形式，因而也是四种对价格形成机制的不同社会学解释。

A first conception of embedding is developed by those according to whom markets can be likened to webs of social relations between agents. Prices depend on the play and strategy of influence, power, or mimesis structured by these social networks.
They are determined by the structure of the relations established between agents.
第一种嵌入观由这样一些人提出：在他们看来，市场可以比作行动者之间的社会关系之网。价格取决于由这些社会网络所结构化的影响、权力或模仿的游戏与策略。
价格由行动者之间所建立的关系结构决定。
In his study devoted to open-outcry auction stock markets,

sociologist Wayne Baker shows the direct impact of network structure on price formation and price levels. His investigation of the stock option markets starts from an observation that goes against what standard economic theory asserts. According to the latter, bigger markets are supposed to be more competitive than smaller ones, and greater competition should attenuate price volatility. However, in Baker’s study, the opposite happens: in the market with the most actors (seventy-one, on average, per observation) there is high volatility, whereas on the smaller one (twenty-seven actors on average, per observation) volatility is low.
在专门研究公开喊价拍卖股票市场的一项研究中，
社会学家韦恩·贝克（Wayne Baker）展示了网络结构对价格形成与价格水平的直接影响。他对股票期权市场的考察，始于一个与标准经济理论的主张相悖的观察。按照后者，更大的市场应当比更小的市场更具竞争性，而更强的竞争应当减弱价格波动。然而，在贝克的研究中，情况恰恰相反：行动者最多的市场（每次观察平均七十一个）波动性很高，而较小的市场（每次观察平均二十七个行动者）波动性则很低。

Baker explains this phenomenon by showing that the quoted values of options depend on the number of participants. When it is low, everyone interacts with everyone, which favors uniformity in evaluations and stabilizes prices. When participation increases, the communication networks stretch out and fragment. Different agents do not compare either the information they have or their evaluations, so prices spread and are more volatile.
贝克通过表明期权的报价取决于参与者数量来解释这一现象。当参与者数量较少时，每个人都与所有人互动，这有利于评价趋同，并使价格稳定。当参与者增多时，沟通网络延伸开来并发生碎片化。不同的行动者既不比较各自掌握的信息，也不比较各自的评价，于是价格离散，波动更大。

Social-network research calls into question the oversimplified relationship between an increase in the number of agents and the intensity of competition. It underlines that supposedly independent agents are actually connected and that these interrelations impose their logic. The importance of networks is a question that economic sociology has explored very systematically. Mark Granovetter’s foundational work shows that in the case of the labor market, the networks and their morphology determine the relations between supplies and demands and thereby influence salary levels.

In a now-classic study devoted to big corporate law firms, Brian Uzzi and Ryon Lancaster discovered, through a sophisticated statistical analysis, that the stronger and more numerous the connections between firms and clients, the lower the prices of legal services.

Looking at producer markets, Harrison White proved that to affix their prices and their production volumes, as well as to maximize revenues, companies observe their competitors’ behavior through their own clients. The strategies companies follow to set their prices are then determined by the structure of their closest relationships, corresponding to what are called niche markets.
Once again, the network acts, but here it is reduced to its local dimension.
社会网络研究质疑了行动者数量增加与竞争强度之间那种过分简单化的关系。它强调，那些被认为是独立的行动者实际上是相互连接的，而这些相互关系强加自己的逻辑。网络的重要性是经济社会学已经非常系统地探讨过的问题。马克·格拉诺维特（Mark Granovetter）的奠基性研究表明，就劳动力市场而言，网络及其形态决定了供给与需求之间的关系，并由此影响工资水平。
在一项如今已成为经典的研究中，布莱恩·乌齐（Brian Uzzi）与瑞安·兰卡斯特（Ryon Lancaster）通过对大型商事律师事务所的复杂统计分析发现，事务所与客户之间的联系越强、越多，法律服务的价格就越低。
哈里森·怀特（Harrison White）在考察生产者市场时证明，为了确定价格与产量并实现收入最大化，公司会通过自己的客户来观察竞争对手的行为。于是，公司为定价所遵循的策略，便由它们最密切的关系结构所决定，这种结构对应于所谓的利基市场（niche markets）。
网络再一次行动了，但在这里它被化约为其局部维度。

Turning to social networks in order to study markets is widespread, and there are numerous other examples I could cite. From the sociologist’s (or economist’s) point of view, the reference structure is still the bilateral transaction —that is the point from which all of these studies begin. However, instead of attending to the competitive pressure generated by agents as a function of their number, sociologists introduce an intermediary variable that changes the shape and effects of this pressure. They abandon an unrealistic hypothesis according to which an undifferentiated population of more or less numerous agents chooses either to cooperate or to act alone. The scene is instead one in which the population is structured by interconnections, exchanges, and power relations. It is these networked interdependencies, and not merely the number of participants, that account for the intensity and the nature of competitive pressure and its effects on prices. The network structure prevails, tempering demographic pressure by shaping the circulation of information. Nevertheless, whether one counts agents or considers the networks they form, in both cases, the bilateral transaction serves as the firm point of departure for the analysis of prices.

借助社会网络来研究市场十分普遍，我还可以举出许多其他例子。从社会学家（或经济学家）的角度看，参照结构仍然是双边交易——所有这类研究都从这一点出发。然而，社会学家并不关注由行动者数量所产生的竞争压力，而是引入一个中介变量，它改变了这种压力的形态与效果。他们放弃了一个不切实际的假设：一个由数量或多或少的行动者组成、内部无差别的群体，会选择合作或单独行动。取而代之的场景是：这个群体由相互连接、交换与权力关系所结构化。正是这些网络化的相互依赖——而不仅仅是参与者的数量——说明了竞争压力的强度与性质及其对价格的影响。网络结构占据主导地位，它通过塑造信息的流通来调节参与者数量带来的压力。然而，无论是清点行动者的数量，还是考察他们所形成的网络，在两种情况下，双边交易都是价格分析的坚实出发点。
Through a second concept of embedding introduced by sociologists, markets can be seen as specific force fields.

The very notion of a market, with the unrealistic hypothesis that there would exist autonomous and separate supplies and demands, is a pure fiction. In reality, as Pierre Bourdieu asserts, prices do not adjust automatically. They are the result of the power relations associated with the positions occupied by agents in the economic field.

Dominant agents are well aware of this: from their point of view, the fiction of competitive markets, which some intellectual or political authorities (such as official committees and think tanks advising decision makers or regulatory agencies fighting unfair monopolies) aim to establish at all costs in order to neutralize power relations, is a very real threat.

What would a company in a monopoly situation have to gain from the implementation of rules that rigorously open the markets to competition? Its interest would be, on the contrary, to maintain the spontaneous tendency of real markets to paralyze competition. Hence, for instance, multinational companies deploy strategies in order to impose
numerus clausus
(“closed number,” limiting those involved, for example, in cartels or in situations of collusion) so as to ensure that prices are essentially determined by the balance of power.
通过社会学家引入的第二种嵌入概念，市场可以被视为特定的力场（force fields）。
市场这一概念本身，连同其关于存在着自主而彼此分离的供给与需求的不切实际假设，纯粹是一种虚构。实际上，正如皮埃尔·布迪厄（Pierre Bourdieu）所断言的，价格并不会自动调整。它们是权力关系的结果，而这些权力关系与经济场域中行动者所占据的位置相关联。
占据支配地位的行动者对此十分清楚：在他们看来，竞争市场这一虚构乃是一种非常现实的威胁——某些知识权威或政治权威（例如为决策者提供建议的官方委员会与智库，或打击不公平垄断的监管机构）力图不惜一切代价确立这种虚构，以中和权力关系。
一家处于垄断情境的公司，能从严格开放市场竞争的规则实施中得到什么好处呢？相反，它的利益在于维持现实市场使竞争瘫痪的自发倾向。因此，例如，跨国公司部署各种策略，以强加“限额”（
numerus clausus
，字面意为“封闭的数目”，即限制参与——例如参与卡特尔或共谋情境——的人数），从而确保价格基本上由力量平衡决定。

The description of markets that these sociological analyses offer is, on the factual level, close to the one provided by industrial economics as it developed in the 1970s, with notions of market structure and monopoly power, linked, for instance, to the erection of barriers to entry or to the development of economies of scale or of scope.
Economic agents are in a permanent struggle to occupy and keep dominant positions, opposing by all possible means the advent of a wider competition that would challenge their incomes.
这些社会学分析所提供的市场描述，在事实层面上，接近于20世纪70年代发展起来的产业经济学所提供的描述：后者带有市场结构与垄断势力的概念，这些概念例如与进入壁垒的设立、或与规模经济或范围经济的发展相联系。
经济行动者处于一场持久的斗争之中，以占据并保持支配位置，用一切可能的手段反对更广泛的竞争的到来，因为这种竞争会挑战他们的收入。

A third conception of embeddedness considers markets to be institutions shaped by rules, conventions, or norms. The organization of competition and its management can be regulated in such a way as to eliminate or attenuate the risks of impediments to competition, such as those that result from collusion and price agreements. Regulation can impose quality standards or a minimum wage, define intellectual property rights, or determine how externalities are taken into account, which is the case when environmental or labor safety laws are enacted. The list goes on: regulation can define classifications and appellations contrôlées (in France, controlled product designations) that aim to make the qualities of goods increasingly visible and less ambiguous; there can be legislation concerning taxes and excises, as well as on the modes of calculating or levying them; an agency can affix key interest rates. Whether public powers or private agents initiate their elaboration, all of these regulations have an impact, direct or indirect, on price levels. Once they are stabilized and regularly implemented, as in the cases of taxes, environmental rules, or collective wage agreements, they can become routinized, some subsets of which can be taken care of by algorithms and integrated software in the pricing procedures.

第三种嵌入观把市场视为由规则、惯例或规范所塑造的制度。竞争的组织及其管理可以被规制，以消除或减弱妨碍竞争的风险，例如由共谋与价格协议所产生的风险。规制可以强加质量标准或最低工资，界定知识产权，或决定如何计入外部性——当环境法或劳动安全法颁布时便是如此。这份清单还可以继续：规制可以界定各种分类与受控原产地命名（appellations contrôlées，法国对产品的受控命名），旨在使物品的品质越来越可见、越来越不含糊；可以有针对税与消费税的立法，以及关于其计算或征收方式的立法；某个机构可以确定关键利率。无论这些规制是由公共权力还是私人行动者发起制定的，它们都对价格水平产生直接或间接的影响。一旦它们稳定下来并被常规施行——如税收、环境规则或集体工资协议的情形——就可能变得例行化，其中的某些子集可以由算法与集成软件在定价程序中加以处理。

Finally, there is a very wide and very loose vision of embeddedness. A fourth way of explaining price levels is to make them depend (at least in part) on agents’ sets of values and therefore on the global cultural determinations that shape their preferences. These determinations may go so far as to push some agents to refuse the commodification of certain goods for reasons often described as ethical.
最后，还有一种非常宽泛、也非常松散的嵌入观。解释价格水平的第四种方式，是使价格（至少部分地）取决于行动者的价值集合，因而取决于塑造其偏好的总体文化规定。这些规定甚至可能促使某些行动者以常被称为伦理的理由，拒绝某些物品的商品化。

In sum, no matter how it defines embeddedness, economic sociology refuses to believe in the possibility of commercial transactions that totally escape power relations. Sheer numbers do not change anything. When two agents are face to face, even if they are surrounded by a multitude of disconnected agents who transform the market into a pure calculating machine, the invisible, but decisive crowd of social relations slips in. They take the form of networks, fields, regulation systems, or cultural determinations. These relations, which bring all their weight to bear on the encounter, preexist and format it in irreversible ways. In a way, economic sociology is only a footnote to Weber’s famous assertion: “Money prices are the product of conflicts of interests and of compromises; they thus result from power constellations.”

总之，无论经济社会学如何界定嵌入，它都拒绝相信存在完全逃脱权力关系的商业交易。单纯的数量改变不了任何东西。当两个行动者面对面时，即便他们周围环绕着众多彼此不相连的行动者、把市场变成一台纯粹的计算机器，社会关系那看不见却具有决定作用的群体仍会潜入其中。它们采取网络、场域、规制系统或文化规定的形式。这些关系把全部重量压在相遇之上，先行存在，并以不可逆的方式塑造了它。从某种意义上说，经济社会学只是为韦伯那句著名论断作的一条脚注：“货币价格是利益冲突与妥协的产物；因此，它们产生于权力格局。”
CONTRIBUTIONS AND LIMITS
The microeconomic approach rightly emphasizes that pricing can and must give rise to a
distributed

(calculation) process, which is indistinguishable from the market. When there are many agents, the market, thus conceived, resembles a squad of very simple robots (they are only asked to establish thresholds), collectively performing better than a small number of complex robots, which would be quite incapable of facing up to the difficulty of the operations required. The market as a whole has more developed cognitive capacities than those of two agents engaged in a bilateral transaction. Without entering into the debate about the efficiency or efficacy of competitive markets, points I will return to in Chapter 8, what should be noted is that in this model, prices are formed in a calculation space peopled by numerous and different agents who are localized in a multitude of dispersed sites and who each contribute,
nolens volens
, to the formation of observable prices. This is the main lesson of economic theory.
贡献与局限
微观经济学进路正确地强调，定价可以而且必须引发一个
分布式

的（计算）过程，这个过程与市场无法区分。当行动者众多时，如此构想出来的市场就像一队非常简单的机器人（只要求它们设定阈值），其集体表现优于少数几个复杂的机器人——后者完全无力应对所需操作的难度。作为整体的市场，比参与双边交易的两个行动者拥有更发达的认知能力。我不打算介入关于竞争市场效率或效力的争论（我将在第八章回到这些要点），此处应当指出的是：在这一模型中，价格是在一个计算空间中被形成的，这个空间里挤满了众多不同的行动者，他们分布在大量分散的场所，每个人
无论情愿与否
，都为可观察价格的形成作出了贡献。这是经济理论的主要教益。

Sociology, in its sometimes fratricidal struggle against microeconomic theory, underlines that neither agents nor markets are free in their calculations. Granted, the process that leads to affixing prices is distributed, but it is embedded in, managed, and oriented by networks of interdependencies, norms, or power relations that determine the result. Pricing is a collective movement that mobilizes a multitude of agents connected to one another as though, on the site where the transaction takes place and at the moment it is concluded, a throng of other sites weighed in on its outcome. Regulations, relations of domination, cultural impregnations, constraints relayed by networks of relations — all of these collective structurings of commercial action explain why
Ps
and
Pb
and the modes of sharing
G
cannot be pushed outside the framework of the market and must therefore be
internalized
in market functioning.

社会学在与微观经济理论有时近于同室操戈的斗争中强调，行动者与市场在计算上都不自由。诚然，导致价格确立的过程是分布式的，但它嵌入于、受管于并由相互依赖的网络、规范或权力关系所引导，而这些决定了结果。定价是一场集体运动，它动员众多彼此相连的行动者，仿佛在交易发生的地点、在交易达成的时刻，还有一大群其他地点对其结果施加了影响。规制、支配关系、文化浸染、由关系网络传递的约束——商业行动的所有这些集体结构化，解释了为什么
Ps
与
Pb
以及
G
的分配方式不能被推到市场框架之外，因而必须被
内化
于市场的运作之中。

In these models, the practices leading to what is called price formation are distributed and internalized. These are two essential results that I will try to capture in the notion of price formulation. This will be possible, however, only by taking positions that are the completely in reverse of the work that has just been presented. The preceding analyses postulate that prices are dependent variables determined, in one case, by the conjoined play of individual preferences and competition, in the other by social relations or social structures. The most extreme and least theoretical form this method takes is the statistical analysis of the different parameters that explain price levels. What happens in a commercial transaction and in fact in each bilateral transaction is determined by a general context, by a constellation of factors that can be grasped through a set of variables that can account for the price in a particular place, at a particular moment, as long as the variables are appropriately chosen. The practices and strategies for pricing that different agents deploy are bracketed out, since it is postulated that these practices do no more than take note of, shape, and transmit the influence of contextual or structural forces.

在这些模型中，导向所谓价格形成的各种实践既是分布式的，也是被内化的。这是两个根本性的结果，我将试图用价格构式这一概念来把握它们。然而，要做到这一点，必须采取与刚刚呈现的研究完全相反的立场。此前的分析假定，价格是因变量：在一种情况下由个体偏好与竞争的共同作用所决定，在另一种情况下由社会关系或社会结构所决定。这种方法最极端、理论性最弱的形式，就是对解释价格水平的各种参数进行统计分析。商业交易中发生的事情——实际上，每一笔双边交易中发生的事情——由一般情境决定，由一组因素决定；只要变量选择得当，就可以通过一组变量来把握这些因素，从而说明某一地点、某一时刻的价格。不同行动者所部署的定价实践与策略则被悬置一旁，因为人们假定，这些实践不过是在记录、塑造并传递情境力量或结构力量的影响。

In the model of market agencements that I am presenting, these practices are on the contrary absolutely central to the analysis. Prices are not mere dependent variables that arrive at the end of the road. They are at the heart of the mechanisms that organize the conjoined transformation of goods and agencies and prepare their singularization. Before introducing the notion of price formulation that makes this reversal possible, I invite the reader to devote a few minutes to research on wine markets, one of the best attempts at compromise between the methods of economics and sociology. What I seek to show with this example is that the distinction between the objective dimension and the symbolic dimension of goods to which this compromise leads nevertheless fails to take into account the reality captured by market agencements.

在我所呈现的市场装配模型中，这些实践恰恰相反，处于分析的核心。价格并不是在道路尽头才出现的单纯因变量。它们处于诸多机制的核心，这些机制组织物品与能动者的共同转化，并为二者的独一化作准备。在引入使这一颠倒得以可能的价格构式概念之前，我请读者花几分钟关注葡萄酒市场研究——这是经济学方法与社会学方法之间最好的折衷尝试之一。我想借这个例子表明：这种折衷所导致的、在物品的客观维度与象征维度之间作出的区分，仍然未能顾及市场装配所捕捉的现实。
THE PRICE OF FINE WINES: WHY IT’S IMPOSSIBLE TO DISTINGUISH THE SYMBOLIC FROM THE MATERIAL DIMENSIONS OF GOODS

The market for high-end wines is one of economic sociology’s favorite topics. For sociologists, as indeed for economists, it is a huge challenge to explain how prices are formed for this market. In these models, the sensory qualities of the wines cannot be the only factors that explain prices. First, because experts very often disagree with one another and regularly revise their judgments as the wine ages.

Second, because the differences in observed prices are not due to the objective properties of the goods or to asymmetric distribution of information about these properties. As Jens Beckert explains, two bottles of wine may be sold at prices that range from a few euros to more than three hundred euros, despite the fact that the chemical characteristics of their content are very similar and despite the fact that data on them are widely available.
上等葡萄酒的价格：为何无法区分物品的象征维度与物质维度
高端葡萄酒市场是经济社会学最钟爱的主题之一。无论对社会学家还是对经济学家来说，解释这个市场的价格如何形成，都是一项巨大挑战。在这些模型中，葡萄酒的感官品质不可能是解释价格的唯一因素。首先，因为专家们常常彼此意见不一，并随着葡萄酒的陈年而定期修正自己的判断。
其次，因为观察到的价格差异并非源于物品的客观属性，也非源于关于这些属性的信息的不对称分布。正如延斯·贝克特所解释的，两瓶葡萄酒的售价可能从几欧元到三百多欧元不等，尽管其内容物的化学特征非常相似，也尽管关于它们的数据广泛可得。

Beckert rightly points to the myriad intermediaries who itemize, compare, establish hierarchies of, and evaluate what they deem to be the intrinsic qualities of the wine, thus contributing to how their prices are established. Jumbled together, they include experts, distributors, journalists, amateur wine clubs, organizers of wine tastings, and of course, influential wine critics who produce buying guides such as Parker’s or Hachette’s. All of these intermediaries, equipped with measuring instruments and evaluation protocols, put into words, conceive elements of language, develop categories, and circulate discourses that are addressed almost exclusively to those who have the resources and cultural codes that give access to the social game of evaluation. Beckert explains that the essential difference between the six-euro bottle and the bottle at 120 euros is generated by this intermediary milieu and the social rankings it enacts. The proof of this is to be found in sales statistics: those who are richly endowed with cultural and economic capital buy the 120-euro bottles; those who are poorly endowed pick up the six-euro bottles.

贝克特正确地指出，有无数中介者对他们认定为葡萄酒内在品质的种种特征进行逐项列举、比较、排序和评价，从而参与决定葡萄酒的价格如何确定。这些中介者混杂在一起，包括专家、分销商、记者、业余葡萄酒俱乐部、品酒会组织者，当然还有颇具影响力的酒评家——他们编写帕克（Parker）或阿歇特（Hachette）之类的购买指南。所有这些中介者都配备测量工具与评价规程，他们诉诸言辞，构想语言要素，发展分类范畴，并传播各种话语；这些话语几乎只面向那些拥有资源与文化符码、因而得以进入这场评价的社会游戏的人。贝克特解释说，六欧元的酒与一百二十欧元的酒之间的本质差别，是由这个中介环境及其所实施的社会排序所生成的。销售统计可以证明这一点：文化资本与经济资本丰厚的人购买一百二十欧元的酒；资本匮乏的人则拿起六欧元的酒。

Certain sociologists or economists easily move from this peculiar observation to the idea that it is possible to draw an analytic distinction between two types of markets. In the first type of market, the quality of the goods can be measured by their material characteristics, which can be easily objectified, are difficult to contest, and around whose appreciation social agreement coalesces. Consumers take the properties of these goods as givens. Beckert suggests referring to these as
standards markets

. In the second type of market, products put in play qualities that are aesthetic or related to taste, moral content, or elements of social status. In these cases, the qualities are subject to controversial judgments; assessments diverge. Real markets, adds Beckert, mix these two components in varying proportions. Everything does have a material value (let us call this a functional and objective value),

as well as a value that sociologists like to call symbolic — that is, subjective and socially constituted. Logically, therefore, the value that prices measure must be a composite value that combines these two components. Economic theory helps to understand how the objective component is constituted. To explain real prices, however, one cannot forget to take the symbolic dimension into account, since through a complex and sophisticated interaction of intermediaries, it weighs in on prices, producing and reproducing status differences both among producers and among consumers. The more intermediaries, the more diversified and professionalized they are, the more important the symbolic component becomes.
某些社会学家或经济学家会轻易地从这一独特观察转向这样一种想法：可以在两类市场之间作出分析性区分。在第一类市场中，物品的品质可以通过其物质特征来衡量；这些特征易于客观化，难以争辩，围绕对它们的评价会凝聚起社会共识。消费者把这些物品的属性当作既定事实。贝克特建议将这类市场称为标准市场（
standards markets
）。在第二类市场中，产品所调动的是审美性的品质，或与品味、道德内容、社会地位要素相关的品质。在这些情形中，品质会招致有争议的判断；评价彼此分歧。贝克特补充说，现实市场以不同比例混合这两种成分。任何东西确实都有一种物质价值（我们不妨称之为功能性的、客观的价值），
也有一种社会学家喜欢称为象征的价值——即主观的、由社会构成的价值。因此，从逻辑上说，价格所衡量的价值必定是一种结合了这两种成分的复合价值。经济理论有助于理解客观成分是如何构成的。然而，要解释现实价格，就不能忘记把象征维度纳入考虑，因为它通过中介者之间复杂而精巧的互动，对价格施加影响，在生产者群体内部以及消费者群体内部生产并再生产地位差异。中介者越多，越多样、越专业化，象征成分就变得越重要。

The distinction between objective and symbolic characteristics makes it possible to explain how pricing mechanisms contribute to perpetuating relationships of domination between economic agents. Developing the symbolic qualities of a wine is costly. Indeed, it requires important investments, among other things, in technology (eliminating pesticides, hand picking the grapes, micro-oxygenation, new oak barrels), in choosing small, well-situated plots, in differentiated access to networks of critics and methods of commercialization, or in the choice and control over marketing tools. These investments, the way they are chosen and implemented, provide fodder for the host of intermediaries who collectively contribute to evaluating wines and establishing a hierarchy among them. Prices, adds Beckert, are indexed to these hierarchies and by the same token become themselves powerful tools of social discrimination. At the top of the scale, one finds producers with sufficient resources to invest in the symbolic dimension and the networks of intermediaries that feed it, courting consumers who are financially and culturally capable of entering the collective evaluation game: the “good” wines go to them. At the bottom of the scale, one finds the producers who simply produce hectoliters and consumers condemned to wines cheaper in price because these have been judged by poorly qualified intermediaries or, worse, are not even worth talking about. The impecunious drinker is mystified. The wine he is drinking is not chemically or biologically different; it is symbolically devalued. Like Siegfried when he accepts the cup containing the potion that will make him forget Brunhild, members of lower classes may think they are drinking wine, but actually they must be drinking to forget how dominated they are! And as they empty their glasses, they are accepting this domination.

客观特征与象征特征之间的区分，使人能够解释定价机制如何助长经济行动者之间支配关系的延续。发展一款葡萄酒的象征品质代价高昂。确实，这需要大量投资，其中包括技术方面的投资（消除农药、手工采摘葡萄、微氧处理、新橡木桶），选择位置优越的小块园地，以差异化方式接触酒评家网络与商业化渠道，或者选择并控制营销工具。这些投资、其选择与实施方式，为大批中介者提供了养料，而他们共同参与评价葡萄酒并在其间建立等级。贝克特补充说，价格与这些等级挂钩，并因此本身也成为社会区隔的有力工具。在这一等级序列的顶端，是拥有足够资源、能够对象征维度以及为其提供养料的中介者网络进行投资的生产者，他们迎合那些在财务上与文化上有能力进入这场集体评价游戏的消费者：“好”酒归于这些人。在这一等级序列的底端，则是只按百升计生产葡萄酒的生产者，以及那些注定只能喝较便宜葡萄酒的消费者——因为这些酒要么由资历不足的中介者评判，要么更糟，根本不值一提。囊中羞涩的饮者受到了蒙蔽。他所喝的葡萄酒在化学或生物学上并无不同；它是在象征层面被贬低了。就像齐格弗里德（Siegfried）接过那杯含魔药的酒、饮下便会忘记布伦希尔德（Brunhild）一样，下层阶级的成员可能以为自己是在喝酒，但实际上，他们必定是在借酒忘记自己受支配的程度！而当他们喝干杯中酒时，他们便是在接受这种支配。

Should we preserve this idea of a symbolic dimension of goods, which provides an elegant explanation for how prices are established and how they participate in power relations? Beckert answers in the affirmative. According to him, this is all the more important because in our affluent societies, functional needs (linked to the usefulness of goods and to their objective characteristics) have basically been satisfied: the way goods are appreciated is increasingly connected to their symbolic dimension. Beckert encourages us to learn to decipher the wine market or the art market in such a way as to pay attention to distinguishing material and symbolic values in order to be better equipped for understanding the markets of the future.
我们是否应当保留物品具有象征维度这一观念？它为价格如何确定、如何参与权力关系提供了一种优雅的解释。贝克特给出了肯定回答。在他看来，这一点尤为重要，因为在我们这些富裕社会中，功能性需求（与物品的有用性及其客观特征相关）基本上已经得到满足：物品被赏识的方式越来越与其象征维度相联系。贝克特鼓励我们学会解读葡萄酒市场或艺术市场，以便注意区分物质价值与象征价值，从而更有能力理解未来的市场。

Beckert’s interpretation ultimately rests on the hypothesis that for any good, it is possible to draw a distinction between intrinsic (material) qualities and external (social or symbolic) qualities. The former are the outcome of material operations that happen before the good is put on the market, while the latter result from symbolic operations that are constitutive of market functioning. Wine is a chemical and biological substance that comes to be seasoned and pepped up with properties that, having been produced by the milieu of intermediaries mentioned above, do not originate in the wine itself, but in the social milieu through which it circulates and in the innumerable stories told about it. Symbolic qualities are to objective qualities what dressing is to salad.

贝克特的解释最终建立在一个假设之上：对于任何物品，都可以区分内在（物质）品质与外在（社会或象征）品质。前者是在物品被投放市场之前发生的物质操作的结果，后者则源于构成市场运作的象征操作。葡萄酒是一种化学与生物的物质，随后被调味、被添料，添上种种属性；这些属性由上述中介者环境生产出来，其来源并不在葡萄酒本身，而在它所流通其中的社会环境，以及关于它所讲述的无数故事。象征品质之于客观品质，正如沙拉酱之于沙拉。

This way of looking at things does not correspond to the reality that is captured by the model of market agencements. Over the course of the previous chapters, we have established that goods are processes, sociotechnical assemblages that are formed and transformed throughout their careers. This is why it should be impossible to think of wine at any point in its career in terms merely of chemical or biological characteristics that would constitute a substrate to which sociocultural or symbolic characteristics might later be added, like successive layers deposited by a 3-D printer. The choice of site, the style in which the vineyard is organized, the history of the land and the region, the conditions of exposure to sunshine, the decision to use oak barrels or not, the modalities of ageing of the wine, the design of the labels, the shape of the bottle, and the circuits through which it is commercialized — none of these are external to the wine. These elements are not there simply to feed the machine that produces social distinctions. They constitute the weft and the substance of “wine” as a product, not so much because they determine its objective properties (for instance, this much exposure to sun producing this number of degrees of alcohol), but simply because their association composes a dense nexus of qualities that defines the product (see Chapter 2), just as so-called chemical qualities do.

这样一种看待事物的方式，与市场装配模型所捕捉的现实并不相符。在前几章中，我们已经确认，物品是过程，是在其整个生涯中不断形成并转化的社会技术集合体。因此，在葡萄酒生涯的任何时点上，都不应只用化学或生物特征来设想它——仿佛这些特征构成一个基底，随后可以在其上添加社会文化或象征特征，就像3D打印机逐层沉积那样。园地的选择、葡萄园组织的方式与风格、土地与产区的历史、日照条件、是否使用橡木桶的决定、葡萄酒陈酿的方式、标签的设计、瓶身的形状，以及它进入商业流通的渠道——这些无一外在于葡萄酒。这些要素的存在，并不只是为了给那台生产社会区隔的机器提供原料。它们构成了作为产品的“葡萄酒”的纬线与实质，这与其说是因为它们决定了葡萄酒的客观属性（例如，如此多的日照产生如此多的酒精度），不如说是因为它们的联合构成了一个界定该产品的密集品质关联（参见第二章），正如所谓的化学品质所做的那样。

Determining the price of the wine is only one step in this qualification process, a profiling process that leads to a finely calibrated adjustment between a good and its buyer. The notion of symbolic value is perhaps only a prosthesis invented to explain the gap between what is supposed to be the real value of the good and its observed price, a bit like the furring that carpenters insert to fill the space between furniture and the walls on which it is fixed. The price, however, is neither the consequence nor the measure of the value of a good. It participates in the formulation of this value, which, as I have shown in the two previous chapters, has no end point. Price is a cause of value, but only one of its numerous causes. The consumer buys the price, just as he buys the exposure to sunshine, the region, of the style of wine making. Turning things around like this frees us from the pressing and insoluble problem that we inherited from classical political economics — namely, the question of connecting price and value.

However laudable it may be, any attempt to reach a compromise between economic and sociological explanations of price formation is bound to be unsuccessful because it fails to acknowledge that the qualification of goods is a process. The only possible strategy for escaping from that dead end is to put pricing practices at the center of one’s analysis. Introducing the notion of price formulation aims to do precisely that.

确定葡萄酒的价格，只是这一品质界定过程中的一步；这一塑形过程导向物品与其买家之间经过精细校准的调适。象征价值这一概念，也许只是一种义肢，被发明出来解释物品所谓真实价值与其可观察价格之间的差距，有点像木匠为填补家具与固定它的墙壁之间的空隙而塞入的垫木。然而，价格既不是物品价值的后果，也不是其衡量尺度。它参与这种价值的构式；正如我在前两章中所表明的，这种价值没有终点。价格是价值的一个原因，但只是其众多原因之一。消费者购买价格，正如他购买日照、产区或酿酒风格。这样把事情颠倒过来，使我们摆脱了从古典政治经济学继承而来的那个紧迫而无解的问题——即如何把价格与价值联系起来。
无论多么值得称道，任何试图在价格形成的经济学解释与社会学解释之间达成妥协的努力，都注定不会成功，因为它未能承认物品的品质界定是一个过程。逃离这一死局的唯一可能策略，是把定价实践置于分析的中心。引入价格构式这一概念，正是为了做到这一点。
PRICE FORMULATION
价格构式
PRICES ARE ALWAYS QUALCULATED FROM OTHER PRICES

To introduce the notion of formulation (and the associated notion of a formula), the simplest approach is to start from an obvious observation: a concrete price is always established on the basis of at least one other price — that is to say, it is only one element in a series of prices that come before and after it. I have known as much since primary school, since we learned the famous rule according to which
sale price = cost price + profit margin

. This rule refers to another operation that makes it possible to establish the cost price from the purchase price and the different costs involved in obtaining the final good and making it available to customers. A little later in my schooling, we were also taught that these operations are false or are as arbitrary as any other convention. (How can one know what the real cost price is? How can one establish precisely what the production costs are?)
价格总是由其他价格质算而来
要引入构式（formulation）这一概念（以及与之相关的公式概念），最简单的进路是从一个显而易见的观察出发：一个具体的价格总是至少依据另一个价格而确立——也就是说，它只是一系列前后相继的价格中的一个要素。我自小学起就懂得这一点，因为我们在学校里学过那条著名的规则：
售价 = 成本价 + 利润额
。这条规则又指向另一项操作，即从进价以及为获得最终物品并使之可供顾客购买所涉及的各种成本，来确定成本价。稍后几年，我们在学校里还学到，这些操作是虚假的，或者与其他任何惯例一样任意。（人们如何能知道真实的成本价是什么？又如何能精确地确定生产成本是多少？）

To say that one cannot know precisely what an objective cost is or could be does not, however, prevent economic agents from spending their time calculating prices and especially calculating them from other prices, which are themselves calculated from other prices. This goes on without it being possible to define either a starting point or an end point. In fact, as economists Gerald Faulhaber and William Baumol noted, the
marking up
technique

remains the simplest, most widespread, and most efficient rule used by supply-side agents to set prices. What is important to my argument right now is not to assess whether this technique is correct or adequate, but to observe that it is used.
Note also that even if cost price is a myth, any company that forgoes precise knowledge of the cost price of its services endangers itself.
One can therefore, paraphrasing economist Piero Sraffa, say of prices what he suggested to say about commodities: they are always made on the backs of other prices.
然而，说人们无法精确知道一种客观成本是什么或可能是什么，并不妨碍经济行动者把时间花在计算价格上，尤其是依据其他价格来计算价格，而那些其他价格本身又是依据另外一些价格计算出来的。这一过程持续进行，既无法确定起点，也无法确定终点。事实上，正如经济学家杰拉尔德·福尔哈伯（Gerald Faulhaber）与威廉·鲍莫尔（William Baumol）所指出的，加价法（
marking up
technique）
仍然是供给侧行动者用来设定价格的最简单、最普遍也最有效的规则。此刻对我的论证而言，重要的不是评判这一方法是否正确或恰当，而是注意到它确实被使用。
还要注意：即便成本价是一个神话，任何放弃精确了解其服务成本价的公司都会使自己陷于危险。
因此，套用经济学家皮耶罗·斯拉法（Piero Sraffa）的说法，我们可以就价格说出他曾建议就商品说出的那句话：价格总是踩在其他价格的背上被造出来的。

WORKING OUT FORMULAS

Before going further into the analysis of price formulation, I will start from an example: the banal example of animal flesh being transformed into a commodity to which a price is assigned. This example will allow me to highlight the material and equipped nature of the work involved in formulation and to identify some of its main characteristics. An attentive examination of the long and tortuous process of the pass(act)ivation of the animal and the transformations it undergoes shows that price formulation is intimately linked to this process, so well described by sociologist Guilhem Anzalone, from whom I borrow the following stylized presentation.
制定公式
在进一步分析价格构式之前，我将从一个例子出发：动物肉体被转化为商品并被赋予价格这一平淡无奇的例子。这个例子将使我能够凸显构式工作之物质性的与装备性的性质，并辨识出它的若干主要特征。仔细考察动物被动化—激活及其所经历诸般转化的漫长而曲折的过程，便会发现：价格构式与这一过程密切相连，社会学家吉扬·安扎隆（Guilhem Anzalone）对此作了出色的描述，下面这份程式化的概述即借自于他。
Anzalone’s analysis centers on the trajectory followed by the meat production process,

from an animal frolicking in a field or moping in a stall to the display case in which flesh, transformed into meat, placed in a container wrapped in cellophane with the proper labeling, awaits a customer who will not shy away from paying the asking price. There are multiple steps along this trajectory, which he analyzes as a stepwise process of deanimalizing, composed of a succession of transformations and (re)qualifications (Chapter 2). Once the beast has been slaughtered, first the skin, guts, head, feet, and spine have to be removed to produce half carcasses. Thus requalified, the animal is ready for a second series of transformations, which, once the muscles have been separated from their membranes, fat, and connected bones, make it possible to group types of meat, which are then vacuum packed. The meat is then “cut,” which means cut into slices to be sold in retail. The last qualification is the presentation in a supermarket of
pieces

whose characterization has been completed with new variables, such as acidity and color, which put the final touch on the qualification of the good offered to the customer. Between the flesh, full of promise, that a trained eye can imagine under the skin of a calf still suckling its mother and the containers lined up in the refrigerated display case, everything has changed and nothing has changed. The same miracle always takes place: operations follow one another, combining the evaluation exercises we met in Chapter 3 into a long series. The result is a kind of transubstantiation.
安扎隆的分析聚焦于肉类生产过程所遵循的轨迹：

从一头在田野里撒欢或在畜栏里蔫头耷脑的动物，直到那个陈列柜——在那里，已化为肉的肉体被装入以玻璃纸包裹、贴有适当标签的容器，等待一位不会因要价而却步的顾客。这条轨迹上有多个步骤，他将其分析为一个逐步去动物化的过程，由一连串转化与（重新）品质界定构成（第二章）。牲畜一旦被宰杀，首先必须去除皮、内脏、头、蹄与脊骨，以制成半胴体。经过这样的重新界定品质，动物便准备好进入第二轮转化：一旦肌肉与其筋膜、脂肪和相连的骨骼分离，就可以把各类肉归并分组，随后进行真空包装。接着，肉被“切割”，也就是切成

以供零售。最后一道品质界定，是在超市中陈列那些肉块——它们的特征描述已经补入了新的变量，如酸度与色泽，这为提供给顾客的物品的品质界定画上最后一笔。在一头仍在吮吸母奶的小牛皮下、训练有素的眼睛所能想象的那种充满潜力的肉体，与冷藏陈列柜中排成一列的容器之间，一切都变了，又什么都没变。同一个奇迹总是在发生：操作一个接一个，把我们在第三章遇到的评价活动组合成一个漫长的序列。其结果堪称一种实体转化（transubstantiation）。

The progressive framings, through separation, dismemberment, and successive cuts, shape entities that start to exist by themselves, detached from their temporary environments to appear ultimately in the form of pieces on display in cellophane. The framings organize the rankings, which establish distinctions between pieces on the basis of multiple variables, both qualitative and quantitative, such as color, part of the animal, texture, and so on. These variables suggest a hierarchy of pieces that can be complex and that can vary according to the criteria and qualities that are taken into consideration. This continuous scoring

work is done at each of the qualification sites by duly equipped intermediaries and professionals in the sector who evaluate the meat as they transform it. At each of these steps and on the basis of a selection of scores and the ordinal scales they offer, intermediate prices,
Pi

, are qualculated with the help of specially conceived formulas. These prices flow together and combine with one another as the transformation process moves forward until a final formula is reached. Summarizing all the others, the final formula provides the

The margins of maneuver are nonnegligible. The decisions and choices the floor managers make are not directly dictated by anyone. They can, for instance, while upholding the framework agreements, set up special promotional offers, as long as they take into account those that are decided at the corporate level so as to avoid contradictions between stores. They can also renegotiate prices with the suppliers. However, their range of action goes beyond these few variables; in France, they intervene between the moment when the ready-to-cut meat arrives on location, piled up in “caddytainers,” large metal crates with multiple shelves on wheels in which the merchandise is stored, and the moment of shelf placement. Consider a floor manager facing one of these caddytainers, which contains five ready-to-cut hindquarters that have to be transformed, unhesitatingly, into a series of labeled trays, each label proclaiming the final price. No human brain, not even the best trained, would be able to perform such a formulation without the help of assistants. The first prosthesis on which the floor manager relies is the caddytainer itself. Indeed, it summarizes and extends the long job of dismembering and evaluating that has been done upstream from the supermarket. The crate itself allows for rapid inspection by grouping together pieces that are qualified as similar: one can imagine how the floor manager would react if suddenly a bouncing, lowing heifer were delivered instead! The second prosthesis on which and with which the floor manager can count is a calculation sheet.

c) A third observation is that via the formulas that establish them, prices establish relations between different evaluation and pricing sites, making them interdependent. Both the structuring of the agencement and the tracing of its borders are a result of the incessant work of constructing relations effected by the different formulas that cross and intersect, making a maze of connections that define the agencement’s contours and constitution. The network of formulas imposes a dynamic on the affixing of prices. It gives rise to multiple exchanges back and forth between the different sites, as well as to iterations, adjustments, and incessant trials and errors. The graft to which Anzalone refers, which means that pricing and qualifying are two entangled processes, starts well upstream from the supermarket stands and well upstream from the slaughterhouses. Prepared for the commercial chain that will lead it to the meat aisle in a supermarket, the cow is a composite being, engaged in several parallel existences from the moment it is born. Its first capers begin to sketch out its sale. When a breeder looks at his herd, he guesses and evaluates the future carcasses that will one day parade in front of the eyes of a “qualitician” — in France, this is the name for a technician in charge of determining quality — who has to decide on the fate of each animal in thirty seconds. Will the shape and thickness of their muscles and their level of fattening allow some of them to move from the status of labelable to prelabeled beasts and later, if the butcher gods are favorable, to that of labeled beef? The animal never ceases to be a real cow, bellowing and quite alive, but its owner raises it so that it is already prepared for what it will become: a dead cow, assemblages of pieces and slices that, after many evaluations, transformations, and formulations, will have to convince customers in a supermarket or a luxury butcher shop; it is a cow whose price flits across its flanks like the retroprojected shadow of slaughterhouse payment schedules or the Excel spreadsheets of floor managers in Romorantin, a small town in the center of France. From the moment of their conception, the animals are simultaneously embedded in several metrological networks, several chains of measuring measures, which, underlining some qualities and amplifying them, make these animals exist both as cows whose characteristics can be found in any encyclopedia and as commodities dispersed in market-price lists. The breeder is not breeding any old cow, but a species that one might call commoditized or commodifiable cattle, the way one speaks of a Normande or Friesian cow. In fact, there are as many profiles of commodifiable cattle as there are possible profiles of their commercial qualities. The number of these new species is not infinite, however, because an ox cannot be eviscerated, cannot be dismembered, cannot be cut up in any old way, even in a purely commercial logic, even if the knife is wielded by the most avid for the immediate profit of capitalists.

c）第三点观察是：价格通过确立它们的公式，在不同评价场所与定价场所之间建立起关系，使这些场所相互依赖。装配的结构化及其边界的勾勒，都是不同公式所进行的、持续不断的关系建构工作的结果；这些公式交错相交，织成一座纵横联结的迷宫，界定了装配的轮廓与构成。公式之网为价格的确定施加了一种动态。它引发不同场所之间多次往返的交换，也引发迭代、调整以及持续不断的试错。安扎隆所说的嫁接——即定价与品质界定是两个相互纠缠的过程——远在超市货架的上游、也远在屠宰场的上游就已经开始。为了那条将把它引向超市肉类货区的商业链条，母牛从出生的那一刻起就是一个复合的存在，同时处于若干平行的实存之中。它最初的蹦跳便开始勾画出它的售卖。当饲养者看着自己的畜群时，他在揣测并评价那些有朝一日将在一名“品质师”（qualitician）眼前列队走过的未来胴体——在法国，这是对负责判定品质的技术员的称呼——而这位品质师必须在三十秒内决定每头动物的命运。它们的肌肉形状与厚度以及肥育程度，是否能让其中一些从“可贴标”的地位转为“预贴标”的牲畜，并随后——如果屠宰之神眷顾——转为“贴标牛肉”？这动物从未停止作为一头真实的母牛而存在，它哞哞叫，生机勃勃；但它的主人饲养它，是为了让它已经为它将要成为的样子作好准备：一头死去的母牛，一堆肉块与肉片的集合体，这些肉块与肉片经过许多次评价、转化与构式之后，必须说服超市或高档肉铺里的顾客；这是一头母牛，其价格在其肋腹上掠动，仿佛屠宰场付款单或法国中部小镇罗莫朗坦（Romorantin）卖场经理的 Excel 表格反向投射的影子。从受孕的那一刻起，这些动物就同时嵌入若干计量学网络、若干“测量之测量的链条”之中；这些网络凸显某些品质并放大它们，使这些动物既作为其特性能在任何百科全书中查到的母牛而存在，也作为分散于市场价格表中的商品而存在。饲养者养的不是随便哪一头母牛，而是一个或许可称为商品化或可商品化牛类的物种，就像人们谈论诺曼底牛（Normande）或弗里斯牛（Friesian）那样。事实上，可商品化牛类的特征构型之多，恰如它们商业品质的可能构型之多。然而，这些新物种的数目并非无限，因为一头牛不能以随便什么方式被掏空内脏、被肢解、被切割，即便在纯粹商业的逻辑下也是如此，即便操刀者是资本家中最贪求眼前利润的人。

Transformed as it moves forward, carried toward its certain destiny, the cow takes on value as it changes state. This commercial destiny lies in an ontological multiplicity that leads to the formulation of the prices at which the final transactions are offered and concluded.

As the cow circulates, it leaves behind a trail of formulating agents. The question being posed is not “What is an animal with such and such characteristics worth?” but rather “What qualities should the animal be given, if it is going to be offered at such and such a price?” The formulation has the double property of maintaining the distributed character of calculations and integrating, internalizing, and summarizing them. Although they are distant, all the different sites are present in the final formulation, which connects and brings them together.
母牛在向前推进中被转化，被带向它确定的命运，并在改变状态的同时获得价值。这一商业命运存在于一种本体论上的多重性之中，正是这种多重性导向对那些最终交易得以报出并达成的价格的构式。
母牛在流通时，留下一道由构式行动者构成的轨迹。所提出的问题不是“一头具有如此这般特征的动物值多少钱？”，而是“如果要按如此这般的价格出售，应当赋予这头动物哪些品质？”构式具有双重属性：既维持计算的分布式特征，又对之进行整合、内化与概括。尽管彼此相距遥远，所有不同场所都出现在最终构式之中，最终构式把它们联结并汇聚在一起。

As a concept, formulation highlights markets’ formidable qualculative power. The usual vision, which takes into account only the relations between supplies and demands, seriously underestimates what makes market agencements so strong — namely, their capacity to organize singular transactions, to aggregate them, and to include pricing in the continual work of adjustment. Supplies and demands matter in the work of formulating prices, but this work does not boil down to observing a ready-made confrontation. Pricing, in the way it has effects on all the sites involved and notably on the process of designing goods and qualifying them, acts from within on the definition of what constitutes supplies and demands and on the qualities of goods offered for sale. In no sense does it measure a state of relations between supplies and demands to which price might be considered external.

作为一个概念，构式凸显了市场令人生畏的质算能力。通常的视角只考虑供给与需求之间的关系，它严重低估了使市场装配如此强大的东西——即它们组织独一交易、把独一交易聚合起来、并把定价纳入持续不断的调整工作的能力。在构式价格的工作中，供给与需求确实重要，但这项工作不能化约为观察一场现成的对峙。定价以其对所有相关场所、尤其是对物品设计与品质界定过程的影响方式，从内部作用于“什么构成供给与需求”的定义，也作用于待售物品的品质。它在任何意义上都不是在衡量一种供给与需求之间的关系状态，仿佛价格可以外在于这种状态。
PRICE FORMULATION SINGULARIZES GOODS
价格构式使物品独一化

Until recently, it was difficult to conceive of prices as simple qualities participating in the singularization of goods. What used to seem absurd now seems obvious. Bespoke, personalized pricing has become common practice, which finally makes explicit that price is never completely external to the good, but that it is in fact one of its essential characteristics. This is accentuated by the widespread development of a particular pricing practice — namely,
yield management
. Indeed, yield management provides a remarkable illustration of the practices involved in price formulation.
直到不久以前，还很难把价格设想为参与物品独一化的单纯品质。过去显得荒谬的事情，如今显得不言自明。量身定制、个性化的定价已成为普遍做法，这终于明确地表明：价格从来不是完全外在于物品的，它实际上是物品的本质特征之一。某一特定定价实践——即收益管理（
yield management
）——的广泛发展，更突出了这一点。的确，收益管理为价格构式所涉及的种种实践提供了出色的例证。
How is the price determined on the ticket I buy for a Paris-Marseille trip? The answer to this question is not straightforward.

The first observation is that since the dawn of railways, prices have always been calculated with the help of formulas. The second is that these formulas have evolved profoundly over time as power relations have changed. The history of this formulation is the painful break from what once seemed obvious: that price should depend on distance traveled. This break unfolded in three stages.
我买一张巴黎—马赛的车票，票价是如何确定的？这个问题并不容易回答。
第一点观察是：自铁路诞生以来，价格一直借助公式来计算。第二点是：随着权力关系的变化，这些公式在时间中发生了深刻演变。这一构式的历史，就是与曾经显得不言自明之事——价格应当取决于所行距离——的痛苦决裂。这场决裂分三个阶段展开。

The second formulation was marginal cost pricing. It appeared as rail transport lost its monopoly, given the increased competition from road transportation. This idea, tried out in socialist economies and introduced in France by Maurice Allais, was to imagine how an efficient market reflects the costs and takes them into account in price formation. All of Allais’s students at the École des Mines in Paris, of whom I was one, remember his famous parable of the passenger at Calais. The question posed was close to the one that interests me here: How much does it cost to have a passenger board the train for Paris at Calais? Allais rightly observed that the existing formula did not bring an acceptable answer to that question. The cost of an extra passenger depends on his order of arrival and depends on the number of passengers who show up. If the train is not full, the additional passengers cost practically nothing, as long as seats are available, but when it is full, the answer is no longer the same! An extra car will have to be added, and then, if the number of passengers continues to increase, a second train will have to be programmed, and finally, if the number of extra trains grows beyond a certain threshold, one will have to consider doubling the tracks. Without going into detailed calculations based on the notion of marginal development cost, it is easy to understand the practical translation of this observation. It leads to taxing certain tickets in order to reduce spikes in demand by inciting those travelers most sensitive to price variations and whose schedules are the most flexible to travel at off-peak hours. This is the principle behind the decision to create a tricolor calendar (blue, white, red) to fill the trains at off-peak hours with senior passengers. The new formula was
Pj = A + D × C ×ϑ(t
), where
D
is the distance between the departure city and the arrival city,
A
a fixed extra tax,
C
a constant corresponding to the price per kilometer,
t
a departure time, and
ϑ
a parameter that varies with the schedule.

第二种构式是边际成本定价。它出现于铁路运输因公路运输竞争加剧而失去垄断之时。这一观念曾在社会主义经济体中试行，并由莫里斯·阿莱（Maurice Allais）引入法国；其要旨是设想一个有效运转的市场如何反映成本，并在价格形成中把成本纳入考虑。阿莱在巴黎矿业学校（École des Mines）的所有学生——我也是其中之一——都记得他那则著名的“加来乘客”寓言。其中提出的问题，与我此处关心的问题十分接近：让一名乘客在加来登上开往巴黎的火车，成本是多少？阿莱正确地指出，既有公式并未对这个问题给出可接受的答案。多载一名乘客的成本，取决于他到来的次序，也取决于实际到场的乘客人数。如果列车没有满员，那么只要还有座位，新增乘客的成本几乎为零；但当列车满员时，答案就完全不同了！必须加挂一节车厢；随后，如果乘客人数继续增加，就必须安排第二列车；最后，如果增开的列车超过某一阈值，就必须考虑把轨道增至双线。无须深入基于边际开发成本概念的具体计算，也不难理解这一观察在实践上的转化。它导致对某些车票加收费用，以减少需求高峰，办法是激励那些对价格变化最敏感、日程最灵活的旅客在非高峰时段出行。正是基于这一原则，才有了设立三色日历（蓝、白、红）的决定，以便在非高峰时段用老年旅客填满列车。新公式为
Pj = A + D × C × ϑ(t)
，其中
D
是出发城市与到达城市之间的距离，
A
是一笔固定的附加费，
C
是对应每公里价格的常数，
t
是出发时间，
ϑ
是随时刻表变化的参数。

The third formulation, however, abandons any reference to distance. One can imagine how counterintuitive it may have been for the SNCF, the Société nationale des chemins de fer français, France’s national railway, to explain to a potential passenger that the price they were going to be charged had nothing to do with how far they were traveling! Is the fact that it costs me more to drive my car from Paris to Nice than from Paris to Bourg-la-Reine in its southern suburbs only an illusion? The SNCF’s answer is yes, and not without good reason. The SNCF explains that the tricolor calendar, which maintains a connection with the distance, is too rigid and does not discriminate enough. The formula is too crude. Since at any given moment, different lines do not have the same occupancy rate, it is absurd to price them in the same way.

然而，第三种构式放弃了任何对距离的参照。可以想见，对法国国家铁路公司（SNCF，Société nationale des chemins de fer français）来说，要向一位潜在乘客解释他所要支付的价格与他出行的远近毫无关系，这该是多么违反直觉！我开车从巴黎到尼斯，比从巴黎到其南郊的布尔拉雷讷（Bourg-la-Reine）花费更多，这难道只是一种幻觉吗？SNCF 的回答是：是的，而且不无道理。SNCF 解释说，三色日历仍然与距离保持联系，过于僵化，区分得不够。这个公式太粗糙了。既然在任何给定时刻，不同线路的载客率并不相同，那么以同样的方式为它们定价就是荒谬的。

The SNCF understood then that an elegant way to hear Allais’s lesson was to consider that purchasing a ticket must be associated with reserving a seat. The verb “to travel,” taken in isolation, does not mean much and says nothing precise about the service rendered; the good is only poorly qualified. What counts is how one travels. The SNCF decided that for the passenger, traveling is not being transported. Traveling means sitting in an assigned a seat. This seat is more or less comfortable; it is available in this or that train, at this time or that; it can be reserved more or less ahead of time; the reservation can or cannot be changed; it can or cannot be canceled without incurring penalties and allowing the customer to opt for another train. Since every seat is different from all the other seats, it is normal and legitimate to pursue this process by attributing a singular price to the seat. It just has to be qualculated. After a fact-finding mission that took them to the United States (by plane), the yield management that the sales agents of the SNCF decided to implement was designed using this approach.

SNCF 当时明白，要优雅地听取阿莱的教诲，一个办法是把购票与订座联系起来。“旅行”这个动词若孤立来看，并没有多少含义，也没有精确说明所提供的服务；物品只得到了拙劣的品质界定。要紧的是如何旅行。SNCF 认定，对乘客而言，旅行并不是被运输。旅行意味着坐在一个被指派的座位上。这个座位或舒适一些，或舒适差一些；它存在于这趟或那趟列车上，在这个或那个时刻；它可以提前较久或较晚预订；预订可以更改，也可以不可更改；可以或不可以在不支付罚金的情况下取消预订、改选另一趟列车。既然每个座位都不同于所有其他座位，那么通过赋予该座位一个独一的价格来推进这一过程，便是正常而正当的。只需对它进行质算。在赴美国（乘飞机）进行了一次实地考察之后，SNCF 的销售人员决定实施的收益管理，正是依照这一进路设计的。

Yield management — selling the right product to the right customer at the right moment and at the right price, the price being simply a quality — is a transposition into practice of the model of discriminating monopolies.
I suggest we now take a detour through this model.
收益管理——在恰当的时刻，以恰当的价格，把恰当的产品卖给恰当的顾客，而价格本身只是一种品质——是把歧视性垄断模型移植到实践中的结果。
我建议我们现在绕道考察一下这个模型。
DISCRIMINATING MONOPOLY AS A REFERENCE SITUATION

A company in a monopoly situation is by definition alone. It has room to maneuver to affix both prices and the quantities offered for sale, although it must adapt to a constraint: the price and the quantity produced must be adjusted to customers’ demand. In the case of a pure monopoly, this constraint corresponds to an intuition based on the self-evident character of the law of supply and demand. If the company decides to increase the volume of its production, it will have to lower the sales price (which is supposed to be unique) so that the demand can absorb the added production. Assuming the company seeks to maximize revenue, we see that beyond a certain threshold and given the diminishing price, the increase in quantity will not bring in additional revenue. This threshold depends on the elasticity of the relationship between demand and price: the less the demand is sensitive to price level, the more the monopoly can increase its income.
作为参照情境的歧视性垄断

一家处于垄断情境的公司，按定义便孑然一身，没有对手。它有回旋余地来同时确定价格与出售数量，尽管它必须适应一项约束：价格与产量必须与顾客的需求相协调。在纯粹垄断的情形中，这一约束对应于一种基于供求规律自明性的直觉。如果公司决定提高产量，它就必须降低售价（售价被假定为唯一的），以便需求能够吸收新增的产量。假定公司寻求收入最大化，我们就会看到：超过某一阈值之后，在价格递减的条件下，数量的增加不会带来额外收入。这一阈值取决于需求与价格之间关系的弹性：需求对价格水平越不敏感，垄断者就越能增加其收入。

To make this analysis compatible with the model of market agencements, we have only to free ourselves from the hypothesis that goods are identical and price is unique. Pricing has to be considered the ultimate phase in the singularization of goods. The reference situation is not one in which a given homogeneous good is supplied to an undifferentiated clientele, but rather one where multiple goods are on offer, proposed at different prices to a population of customers who are themselves different. Every monopoly is considered akin to an assemblage of bilateral monopolies, each corresponding to a unique transaction established between a supply and a demand whose singularization is ensured, at the very least, by a specific price being established.
要使这一分析与市场装配模型相容，我们只需摆脱物品彼此相同、价格唯一这一假设。必须把定价视为物品独一化的最终阶段。参照情境并不是把某种同质物品供应给无差别的顾客群，而是有多种物品在售，以不同价格提供给本身也各不相同的顾客群体。每一种垄断都被视为类似于一组双边垄断的集合，其中每一个双边垄断都对应着供给与需求之间建立的一笔独特交易，而这两者的独一化至少是通过确立一个特定价格而得到保证的。
In the case of a
perfectly

discriminating monopoly, each consumer is identified and characterized by their capacity to pay for the good or service they are offered. Economist Étienne Wasmer thus presents this as the case of a monopoly “that would know at the exact moment when you buy a coffee at the only machine in the cafeteria that is working, how much you are really prepared to pay for the mokaccino. The monopoly . . . will then take all the surplus for each customer.”

The main difference with classical situations of pure monopoly or pure competition is that the prices (of what we used to consider the same good) are not unique, but are instead adapted to each customer. The mokaccino on offer for this customer at this moment in this place is obviously different from the mokaccino on offer elsewhere at another moment to another customer, even if the beverages are comparable.
在
完全
歧视性垄断的情形中，每个消费者都被识别出来，并以其为所获物品或服务付费的能力来加以刻画。经济学家艾蒂安·瓦斯梅（Étienne Wasmer）由此把这种情形描述为一种垄断：“它会在你于自助餐厅唯一一台还能运转的机器前买咖啡的那一刻，确切知道你到底愿意为这杯摩卡奇诺（mokaccino）付多少钱。于是，这种垄断……将从每位顾客身上取走全部剩余。”
它与纯粹垄断或纯粹竞争的古典情境的主要区别在于：价格（那些我们过去视为同一物品的价格）不再是唯一的，而是针对每位顾客加以调整。此时此地提供给这位顾客的摩卡奇诺，显然不同于彼时彼地提供给另一位顾客的摩卡奇诺，即便这些饮料彼此相当。

Between a pure monopoly that knows only a block of demand and is a limit configuration of interface markets and the purely discriminating monopoly that knows only singularities and tips into the world of market agencements, there are a number of intermediary configurations. For instance, blocks of consumers can correspond to a segmentation of the clientele: for each unit sold at the same price to the same type of buyer, the price varies according to the type of buyer as qualified by age, occupation, and so on. What is significant in the analysis I am putting forward is that beyond the description of these imperfections, the reference situation is no longer pure competition or its antithesis, pure monopoly. The reference is now the purely discriminating monopoly — that is to say, an agency that offers only singularized goods for sale at different prices.

一端是只知道一个需求板块、属于界面市场极限构型的纯粹垄断，另一端是只知道独一性、滑入市场装配世界的纯粹歧视性垄断；在这两者之间，存在着若干中间构型。例如，消费者板块可以对应于顾客群的一种细分：对于以同一价格卖给同一类型买家的每一单位，价格随买家的类型而变化，而买家类型则按年龄、职业等来界定。我所提出的分析中具有重要意义的一点是：除了描述这些不完美之处，参照情境不再是纯粹竞争或其对立面——纯粹垄断。如今的参照是纯粹歧视性垄断，也就是说，一个只以不同价格出售独一化物品的能动者。
In the case of a discriminating monopoly, the company has to endow itself with powerful equipment in order to observe the customers (to determine their
Pb
) and effect infinitely more complicated calculations than those of a pure monopoly or companies in situations of oligopoly.

One can no longer say that prices are the result of the meeting of supplies and demands except in a metaphorical manner. Prices are calculated on a case-by-case basis. In order to explain how they are determined, the only available strategy is to carry out an ethnography of pricing to show how in market agencements and over the course of the bilateral transactions they frame each agency operates its own qualculations, taking into account (and internalizing) the (distributed) qualculations realized at other sites by other agencies. Yield management (also called revenue management) is a good starting point for such investigations, which should also pay attention to the knowledge and instruments that are designed, tested, and implemented by pricing professionals.
在歧视性垄断的情形中，公司必须为自己配备强有力的装备，以便观察顾客（确定其
Pb
），并进行远比纯粹垄断或处于寡头情境的公司复杂得多的计算。
人们再也不能说价格是供给与需求相遇的结果，除非是在隐喻意义上。价格是逐案计算出来的。为了解释价格如何确定，唯一可用的策略是开展一种定价民族志，以表明在市场装配中、在它们所框定的双边交易过程中，每个能动者如何运作自己的质算，同时考虑（并内化）其他能动者在其他场所实现的（分布式）质算。收益管理（也称收入管理）是这类研究的一个良好起点；这类研究还应关注定价专业人士所设计、测试和实施的知识与工具。
YIELD MANAGEMENT

A discriminating monopoly is not a fanciful invention. Yield management is its most accomplished practical translation. Until recently, it seemed unrealistic to consider that one could have instantaneous access to the
Pb

of customers. With the arrival of centers of big data that enable the data to be collected and the development of data-processing tools, this is now conceivable. In conjunction with the hypotheses and contributions of behavioral psychology, big data makes it possible to establish profiles and manage the long, costly procedures by trial and error that used to be necessary to reach the
Pb
收益管理
歧视性垄断并非异想天开的发明。收益管理是它最完善的实践转译。直到不久以前，认为人们能够即时获得顾客的
Pb
，似乎仍不现实。随着能够收集数据的大数据中心的出现以及数据处理工具的发展，这如今已是可以设想的了。结合行为心理学的假设与贡献，大数据使得建立用户画像、并管理过去为达到
Pb
所必需的漫长而昂贵的试错程序成为可能。
Yield management has given rise to intense research and experimentation. Management scientist Andrew Boyd’s book gives a good presentation of this work.

He starts by noting that with the resources of big data and the internet, it is time to introduce a bit of science and technology into pricing activities. The market, and with it the law of supply and demand, says Boyd, does not determine much. Prices are established as a result of struggles between agents who try to impose their own qualculations. In this struggle, equipment counts — in both senses of the term. It makes the difference, and, Boyd adds, if suppliers want to optimize their revenues, they have to wrap their heads around the fact that each transaction is a bilateral transaction that requires singular goods offered at prices that are established in a singular way. Supply does not confront
one
demand, but rather a multitude of different potential demands; it can satisfy these only if it disaggregates itself into a multitude of singular offers.
收益管理引发了大量研究与试验。管理学家安德鲁·博伊德（Andrew Boyd）的著作对这项工作作了很好的介绍。

他首先指出，凭借大数据与互联网所提供的资源，现在是时候把一点科学与技术引入定价活动了。博伊德说，市场以及随市场而来的供求规律，并不能决定多少东西。价格是在行动者之间的斗争中确立的，这些行动者力图把自己的质算强加于人。在这场斗争中，装备算数——在这个词的双重意义上都是如此：它既参与计算，也举足轻重，正是它造成差别。博伊德补充说，如果供应商想要优化收入，就必须想明白：每一笔交易都是双边交易，都要求以独一的方式确立的价格提供独一的物品。供给所面对的并不是
一种
需求，而是众多不同的潜在需求；它只有把自己分解为众多独一的供给，才能满足这些需求。

The book presents the formulas and the calculations that allow both for this exploration and for the optimization of revenues. Yield management is a practical application of the theory of discriminating monopolies. It does not simply play on prices, but instead makes prices one of the many qualities that allow goods to be singularized and makes it possible to construct the market as a sum of bilateral monopolies. Which good, for whom, and at what price? These are the questions the supplier must ask, knowing that the answer must take into account a series of constraints and, notably, the fact that the singularization of goods must not lead to an upheaval in design and production activities that would lead to an unreasonable increase in costs.
这本书给出了既可用于这种探索、又可用于收入优化的公式与计算。收益管理是歧视性垄断理论的一种实际应用。它并非仅仅在价格上做文章，而是把价格变成使物品得以独一化的众多品质之一，并使把市场建构为双边垄断之总和成为可能。哪种物品，给谁，以什么价格？这些是供应商必须提出的问题；同时他知道，答案必须考虑一系列约束，尤其是这样一点：物品的独一化不得导致设计与生产活动的剧变，以致成本不合理地上升。

Boyd explains that yield management was imagined by airline companies during the upheaval provoked in the 1980s by deregulation policies that rekindled competition. To face these conditions, they revived the process of singularization, concentrating on what they controlled — namely, how the seats offered to passengers would be qualified. Their personalization, like that of the SNCF seats, can be achieved by attaching characteristics such as the possibility of changing the reservation or not, choosing a position in the aircraft, reserving far ahead of time, selecting the date and time of the flight, and so on. Customers are profiled. This singularization seems slight, but it can be successfully carried out only through a complete overhaul of both sales networks and techniques and the ways reservations are handled. Heavy computational infrastructures, sophisticated algorithms, and data-collecting devices are set up in order to singularize seats and formulate their prices. The material component of these innovations becomes visible when one accepts the idea that a seat is not simply a piece of furniture with armrests and a back. The seat on which the passenger sits includes the systems for reservations and price formulations. These systems have had at least as great an impact on the transformation-requalification process as the invention of assembly-line production in the automobile industry of the 1930s. Before these disruptive inventions, the continuous updating of reservations was a real conundrum, with complicated heavy mechanical systems that depended on constantly sorting perforated cards.

博伊德解释说，收益管理是航空公司在20世纪80年代由放松管制政策所引发、重新点燃竞争的剧变期间构想出来的。为应对这些条件，它们复兴了独一化过程，把注意力集中在它们所能控制的事情上——即如何界定提供给乘客的座位。这些座位的个性化，如同 SNCF 座位的个性化，可以通过附加各种特征来实现，例如能否更改预订、选择在飞机中的位置、提前很早就预订、选择航班的日期与时刻，等等。顾客被画像化。这种独一化看似微不足道，但只有彻底改造销售网络与技术以及预订处理方式，才能成功地实现它。为了独一化座位并构式其价格，人们建立起庞大的计算基础设施、精巧的算法与数据采集装置。当人们接受“座位并不只是一件带扶手和靠背的家具”这一观念时，这些创新的物质成分就变得可见了。乘客所坐的座位包括预订系统与价格构式系统。这些系统对转化—重新界定品质过程的影响，至少与20世纪30年代汽车工业中流水线生产的发明一样大。在这些颠覆性发明之前，持续更新预订是一个真正的难题，要靠不断分拣穿孔卡片的复杂而笨重的机械系统来完成。

Having started in the airline industry, this movement then scattered everywhere, notably into ground transportation such as the railways. More and more companies put scientific pricing into practice. As yield management experts put it, a hotel is just a plane without wings. Thanks to wisely placed sensors, the price of a bottle of Coca-Cola for spectators at an American football game can vary with the temperature of the moment, the hypothesis being that the hotter it is, the more fans are willing to pay for refreshments.
这一运动始于航空业，随后扩散到各处，尤其是铁路等地面运输领域。越来越多的公司把科学定价付诸实践。用收益管理专家的话说，酒店不过是一架没有翅膀的飞机。借助巧妙放置的传感器，美式橄榄球比赛观众买一瓶可口可乐的价格可以随当时的温度而变化；其假设是：天气越热，球迷就越愿意为饮料付钱。

Personalization through pricing is not new, but for a long time, it remained invisible. Boyd describes amusing situations in which the discounts given confidentially to certain customers gave rise to leaks that severely embarrassed producers. Singularizing through pricing was done, but in a clandestine and artisanal fashion. Scientific pricing rationalizes this practice, which becomes a full-fledged object for research and development. Price formulation is henceforth an industry with its platforms, its professional associations, its institutes and training seminars, its university teaching, its conferences, and its particular know-how spiced with a grain of cynicism.
通过定价实现个性化并不新鲜，但长期以来它一直不可见。博伊德描述了一些有趣的情形：秘密给予某些顾客的折扣发生泄漏，令生产者极为难堪。通过定价进行独一化早已有之，只不过是以秘密的、手工业式的方式进行的。科学定价使这种做法理性化，使它成为一个名副其实的研究与开发对象。从此，价格构式成为一门产业，拥有自己的平台、行业协会、研究所与培训研讨会、大学教学、会议，以及一种带有一丝玩世不恭味道的特殊专长。

Inspired by yield management work, most online businesses have recruited entire teams to work on price formulation. These experts process both internal data (the number of items in stock, the age of products) and external data, collecting the prices of hundreds of references on dozens of sites several times a day. They are thus able to follow changes in the supply and in the qualification of the goods on offer, a requalification that includes adjusting the price. The formulas, in the form of algorithms, determine at each moment the price that will maximize margins. In these formulas, elements such as the weather, the hour of the day, whether or not the web surfer has been to a price comparison site, the approach of school holidays, what is on television that evening, or the content of the literary supplements of big newspapers are all variables that may be taken into account. More individual data, such as the brand of the computer (Mac users are presumed to have more money), can also be taken into account in the formulation. The increasing part played by pricing technicians, notably in e-commerce, translates into permanently changing prices. Prices are now dynamic.
